precepts.text: The saying began at Egypt: they will kill me, but save thee alive; say thou art my sister.
precepts.point: Abraham said again, She is my sister, as he had done entering Egypt, for fear the men of the place would kill him for his wife's sake; Sarah was still that fair to look upon even at ninety.
precepts.why:
“She is my sister” was not new in Gerar. It began entering Egypt. Abram said to Sarai, “Behold now, I know that thou art a fair woman to look upon: Therefore it shall come to pass, when the Egyptians shall see thee, that they shall say, This is his wife: and they will kill me, but they will save thee alive. Say, I pray thee, thou art my sister: that it may be well with me for thy sake; and my soul shall live because of thee.”

The fear was the same in Gerar: that the men of the place would kill him for his wife’s sake. And Sarah was still that fair to look upon even at ninety, which is why Abimelech king of Gerar sent and took her.

precepts.text: The Lord plagued Pharaoh and his house with great plagues because of Sarai; it happened both times she was taken.
precepts.point: The same happened with Pharaoh before. The Most High plagues a household over the prophet's wife; He does not play about that.
precepts.why:
Behind the scenes “the Lord had fast closed up all the wombs of the house of Abimelech, because of Sarah Abraham’s wife.” The same thing happened the first time she was taken: “the Lord plagued Pharaoh and his house with great plagues because of Sarai Abram’s wife.”

Both times, the whole house suffered. The Most High plagues a household over the prophet’s wife; He does not play about that. And when Abraham prayed, God healed Abimelech, his wife and his maidservants, and they bare children.

points: Abraham said again, She is my sister, as he had done entering Egypt, for fear the men of the place would kill him for his wife's sake; Sarah was still that fair to look upon even at ninety.

God came to Abimelech in a dream: Behold, thou art but a dead man, for the woman is a man's wife. Adultery was sin in Genesis, way before Exodus 20:14; the Most High said, I withheld thee from sinning against me.
Abimelech had acted in the integrity of his heart, and the Most High withheld him from touching her. Restore the man his wife, for he is a prophet, and he shall pray for thee.
Abimelech called it what it is: a great sin. Adultery is one of the weightier matters; there is no animal sacrifice that atones for it.

Abraham thought, Surely the fear of God is not in this place. And technically she was his sister: the daughter of his father but not of his mother, who became his wife; the sister saying was their agreement in every strange land.
Behind the scenes the Lord had fast closed up all the wombs of the house of Abimelech because of Sarah; when Abraham prayed, God healed them.
